summary: Item one, "Let grapenuts run.", is only partly answered, and the summary says so. Grapenuts ran on Hatteras (33 jobs). A code description is written, and survival, energy and bulk physics against sequel's engine were measured, all on one seed. The phase diagram, the fourth part of the evaluation Chris described, was not started. Item two (unpause, run on Hatteras) is answered. Almost all the work served item one. The stiffness check (E0101) is part of comparing with the baseline, not a side quest. The session proposed no claims. I reviewed its experiments in their place, and the numbers I checked hold. I reran the referee's bulk judge myself (referee/bulk.py baseline, measure and judge on artifacts A0146 and A0138). It reproduces the one failure at stiffness 1e7 exactly: plate contact at +3.80 standard deviations against a 3.62 limit, with the other six quantities within 1.07. One artifact checksum matches its manifest (A0138 summary.json). The run's CPU total of 2.655 hours is the sum of its 30 collected job records. All ten completed spring runs had zero slow episodes, so they never slowed down rather than recovering from a slowdown. Plate springs book plate work as plate velocity times impulse (edmd.py at 486d8eb), so energy can't hide in plate work. Four things are missing or overstated, and Chris should read them before the line's state. (1) The energy books hide a large positive term. The spring dissipation book includes friction work, and grapenuts' own counter of positive friction work (SF_FRICTION_GAIN) totals 0.2 to 2.3 percent of the plate's energy input over each 1e7 run. That is ten to thirty times the net residual the summary reports (4e-5 to 1.8e-3), and larger than the worst single-cycle gain. It can be physical: in the Walton law the slip reverses partway through a contact, so single kicks can do positive work while the whole contact still loses energy. But nobody measured whether any contact gains energy overall. So the line's sentence 'Net energy over each run is a loss' says how well the books close, not that the method injects no energy. The summary and line state never mention this term. (2) E0099's own falsification rule is already met. It was registered as falsified if the residual is positive 'in more than a few cycles'. The evidence shows 16 gaining cycles at Gamma 5, f* 0.3, depth 10 and 8 at depth 5, yet the summary doesn't say the hypothesis has failed. Its outcome is pending only because three jobs are still running. (3) The summary says of sequel's two failed Hatteras baselines 'on your Mac these ran', and proposes checking whether the difference is the machine. The program's own Mac runs (E0031, seeds 1 to 3) argue against that. At Gamma 3.5, f* 0.3, depth 10, seeds 2 and 3 failed on the Mac at cycle 0. At Gamma 5, f* 0.5, depth 5, seed 1 overlapped at cycle 274 on the Mac and seeds 2 and 3 failed too. Failure there is common on any machine, so one seed failing on Hatteras is not evidence the baseline depends on the machine. (4) Small inconsistencies. Blocker B0007's resolution says grapenuts' 'test suite runs locally', but the summary says it never finished locally (it stopped at test 90 of about 139). The summary gives 17 to 24 CPU-seconds per cycle for the unfinished jobs and 0.2 to 24 in 2D, but the evidence has 15.6, 18.5 and 26.1 for the unfinished jobs. The E0101 registration is stamped 02:57:00Z but was committed at 02:56:25Z. Its jobs were submitted after the commit, so pre-registration held. My last review's challenge on term T0032 is answered: T0033 and lines/L0020/grapenuts.md describe springs applied as impulses between free flights, and the kick function at 486d8eb matches. The line's note and state otherwise match the evidence, including 'holds at 1e8 only', which rests on one seed and three conditions; the state says one seed. Housekeeping: program check fails on this branch for a reason that isn't the run's. Chris's signed approval at 03:19:34Z (commit ca3cd20 on main, after the run ended) covers a program.toml with '[service] max_parallel_lines = 4', and line/L0020 doesn't have that commit yet. It also flagged my own scratch folder, which I then deleted. Approvals in the last day: approved/20261123T150635467708Z, approved/20261123T154749869507Z, approved/20261123T154935757398Z and approved/20261124T031934297997Z. The last is an annotated, signed tag naming Chris Bizon. Disk: 92 GB free (floor 40), sequel-data 366 MB (ceiling 15 GB), tmp/ empty apart from an empty fetch folder, and nothing written outside the program folders except tool caches.

answers.finding: The summary copies the item word for word. The Details define the work as the checker looking at the code, a phase diagram, and comparing energies with the baseline. Three of those were done; the phase diagram was not started, so 'partly' is right. The work tested something. The spring runs differ from grapenuts' hard mode at the same conditions: thousands of springs form per cycle, the energy books differ by about 1e-4 against 1e-12, and the bulk judge moves from at most 1.5 standard deviations (hard) to 3.8 (springs). The departures are disclosed and reasonable: a grapenuts-side copy of the referee loop (D0066), and baselines rerun on Hatteras. Two parts of the answer go further than the evidence. 'Over every run the method loses energy on net' leaves out the positive friction work booked inside the dissipation term (0.2 to 2.3 percent of throughput). And 'on your Mac these ran' doesn't fit the program's Mac runs at Gamma 5, f* 0.5, depth 5, where seed 1 overlapped at cycle 274 and seeds 2 and 3 also failed.

answers.finding: The summary copies the item word for word. The line ran on Hatteras: 33 jobs, 30 collected with job records summing to 2.655 CPU-hours, and three still running. Blocker B0007 (the missing clone) is resolved: the clone is at sequel-data/grapenuts with HEAD 486d8eb, and the program's evaluation script is committed there on branch sequel-eval (23a3676). The job records show it ran clean.

run_conditions.assessment: The run started at 02:36Z and ended at 03:16Z, matching its last commit at 03:16:15Z. That is forty minutes, within its hour. It collected 30 of its 33 Hatteras jobs, judged bulk physics at the three conditions that had a baseline, and left three long Gamma 5 jobs (two deep 2D runs and the 3D run) running, as recorded in progress.md. They are waiting only on time. The machine didn't limit the science. What limits it is one seed per condition and two baselines that failed on Hatteras, and the run said both. Budgets are far from their limits: 499 of 10,000 CPU-hours this week (5 percent), the largest job 0.3 CPU-hours against 100 per run, and disk 92 GB free against a 40 GB floor.
discrepancies: Blocker B0007's resolution says grapenuts' test suite 'runs locally', but the summary's limits_hit says it never finished locally (it stopped advancing at test 90 of about 139, twice).

The summary gives 17 to 24 CPU-seconds per cycle for the three unfinished jobs and 0.2 to 24 in 2D. The evidence (E0099-results.json) has 15.6, 18.5 and 26.1 for those jobs, so the 2D maximum is 26.1, not 24.
I couldn't check cores_available (37) or sleep: this container has no uptime or pmset, as the run said. 40 cores (nproc) and the free disk (92 GB) match.
